target_customer: B2B sales and marketing teams, especially small and mid-sized, that want to convert website visitors and intent signals into pipeline
problem: Most B2B website visitors leave unidentified, so sales teams miss warm leads that showed buying intent and fail to follow up fast.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with usage tiers and a free plan
product_category: Revenue orchestration, visitor identification and AI sales agents

founders.name: Max Greenwald
founders.background_notes: YC bio calls him a first time founder.

founders.name: Alan Zhao
founders.background_notes: Met the co-founders at On Deck per YC page.

founders.name: Val Yermakova
founders.background_notes: Named in one directory profile; not on YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Required stitching third party intent data (6sense, Clearbit, Bombora) with identity matching, chat and outreach automation; integration heavy but standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Built on licensed third party data and commodity chat and email tooling; larger vendors could replicate it, and the dependency on data vendors was a risk.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: HubSpot acquired Clearbit and then agreed to acquire Warmly itself, announced 2026-06-30 for undisclosed terms; partners since a 2023 integration.

market_need_then: Pandemic era shift to remote and digital selling in 2020 made website intent and warm lead follow up valuable; company later claimed 100+ paying customers.

branding.name_origin: Sources show the name is written with a trailing comma like an email sign-off; why the company chose Warmly itself is not stated.
branding.domain_note: Uses warmly.ai; earlier aggregator listing uses warm.ly.

identity.logo: Wordmark, not described in detail by sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, with the comma as a deliberate quirk ('Add A Comma')

branding.community_and_virality: Careers page and a 2020 Berkeley Haas profile reference the comma; no evidence of merch or fan content.

brand_strength.rationale: Warm, distinctive name with a memorable comma quirk fitting the warm leads pitch, but no independent evidence it drove growth.

pivots.from: Zoom tool showing names and company details in virtual backgrounds, after earlier cofounder matching ideas
pivots.to: Warm lead identification and follow up for sales teams
pivots.why: Per interview coverage, the founders moved toward supplying sales teams with warm leads; exact date not stated.

outcome_analysis: Warmly pivoted from a Zoom novelty tool to identifying warm B2B leads, raised a seed in 2021, an $11M Series A led by Felicis in October 2023 and a $6M extension in February 2025, then added AI sales agents. HubSpot, a long time integration partner, agreed to acquire it in mid 2026, an incumbent buying a wedge it relied on rather than building it.
notes: Seed amount varies ($2.1M vs $2.4M) between aggregators; the $2.4M figure used. Deal announced June 30, 2026 per trade press, YC page news item dated July 26, 2026; closing status unclear. No competitor source dated 2020 was found; Drift, Clearbit Reveal and Qualified appear only in vendor and competitor blogs from later years, so the list is empty.
